issues.claim: Problem summary: 'A one-year program in which CVSA-certified inspectors replaced driver walkarounds found defects on 1,000+ assets...'
issues.problem: The cited Kodiak post does not say certified inspectors replaced driver walkarounds. It describes a separate CVSA Enhanced Inspections program (a zero-defect certified inspection, valid 24 hours, run for autonomous trucks) and states Kodiak 'already routinely inspected its own assets every day'. 'Replaced' implies the statutory driver walkaround was substituted, which the source does not support and which conflicts with the avenue's own 392.7 point.
issues.fix: Reword to 'a year-long program in which CVSA-certified inspectors performed a stricter zero-defect inspection on top of the existing daily driver inspection'. The measured_outcomes row for the same study is worded correctly and can be reused.

issues.claim: '...the two pass rates are not the same trailers, so treat it as directional evidence' (problem section)
issues.problem: Stated as fact. The source says '70% of trailers from these same partners passed a traditional DVIR' - same partners, but it never states whether the two populations are identical trailer pools, so the assertion is an inference presented as fact.
issues.fix: Label it: 'the source compares partner trailer populations rather than a matched sample (inference), so treat the gap as directional'. The rest of the caveat ('vendor's own account, no independent audit') is accurate and well labeled.

issues.claim: measured_outcomes: Kodiak sample '1,000+ tractor and trailer assets inspected over roughly 12 months'; problem section calls it 'a one-year program'
issues.problem: Minor: the pilot launched April 2023 and the post is dated August 20, 2024 (~16 months of elapsed monitoring). The 'one year' framing follows the vendor's own headline ('One Year In'), so it is defensible but imprecise against the dates in the same source.
issues.fix: Say 'the first ~16 months (pilot launched April 2023; vendor post dated Aug 2024, headlined

issues.problem: All figures are confirmed, but the brief itself notes CargoNet is a commercial data provider that also sells theft-prevention services and that its intake figures are not independently audited - by the same logic applied to Kodiak, this is closer to Low.
issues.fix: Downgrade to Low, or state explicitly why a self-reported commercial incident count rates above a self-reported vendor pilot.

issues.problem: The cited article says inspectors 'found 13,553 violations' without qualifying them as vehicle-only (CVSA-derived sources put total vehicle+driver+HM OOS violations at 17,047, with 10,148 vehicles removed). The label 'vehicle' is a small over-read of the source.
issues.fix: Write '13,553 OOS violations (all categories, per the trade-press reproduction)' or cite the CVSA-derived breakdown that separates vehicle and driver violations.

issues.claim: buyers: Middlesex County 'more than 1,300 warehousing/distribution buildings (NJTPA, built on a 2010 baseline)'
issues.problem: No source_url is attached to this figure anywhere in the brief, so a reader cannot open it, even though the caveats section cites it by name.
issues.fix: Add the URL (njtpa.org Middlesex County Freight Profile PDF, which states 'more than 1,300 warehousing/distribution buildings' for a 2010 baseline) to the buyers entry and to the data_gaps/assumptions note.

issues.claim: fit_score: technical_feasibility 12/15 while the rationale calls technical feasibility 'medium'
issues.problem: Arithmetic is correct (14+13+8+12+8+8 = 63) and legal_risk_low 8/15 matches the 'low-moderate, not low' language, but 12/15 for a capability the brief describes as medium reads high and slightly overstates feasibility relative to the stated 'tread depth, brake adjustment and crack detection are not solved' evidence.
issues.fix: Optional: drop to 10-11 and re-total, or state in one line why 'medium' difficulty still scores 12/15 (detection, tracking and OCR are commodity; only defect adjudication is unsolved).
